(1) Homocysteinylation of the redox-sensitive transcription factor, Nrf2, is an important mechanism for the regulation of Nrf2-dependent gene expression and (2) Homocysteinylated Nrf2 is associated with increased oxidative stress and reduced antioxidant defense in cardiovascular disease.

(1) homocysteinylation and folate deficiency are associated with the development of heart failure, (2) the mechanisms of homocysteination and folate deficiency in the development of heart disease are complex, and (3) the mechanisms of the development of heart diseases are different in men and women.

1) the methionine–homocysteine (Met–Hcy) cycle, folate metabolism, and the redox–methylation balance are tightly linked, 2) a normal redox–methyation balance, or “metoxistasis”, is essential for normal physiology, and 3) a disturbance of methoxyastasis may be a better indicator of cardiovascular disease risk than hyperhomocysteemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the redox-methylenation balance, or methoxistasis, which is coordinated by the methylation-homocysteinethiolation cycle.
understanding how the methionine–homocysteine–folate cycle is regulated and how this regulation is altered in cardiovascular disease.
the regulation of the methionine homocysteene cycle and the role that folate metabolism plays in the regulation of cardiovascular function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

homocysteineaemia, folate deficiency, and the methionine homocysteinaemia cycle are not the cause of cardiovascular disease, but rather the result of a more generalised disturbance in the redox and methoxistasis of the body.
homocysteinaemia is a marker of disturbed methoxistasis, and that the restoration of methoxistatis is the goal of therapy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hyperhomocystinemia is a marker of disturbed methoxistasis, which is a more complex biologic pertubation than a simple elevation of homocysteien level.

the methionine homocysteines cycle is not simply a pathway to produce homocysteins.
